SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #10
====

GRADE: Grade 6
SUBJECT: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   D. A chemical reaction forming ash

2. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 0 °C

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Change of State? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Change of State.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Change of State.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Change of State.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Change of State.

4. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. watt (W)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. newton (N)

5. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Ice melting to water
   C. Iron rusting
   D. Milk souring

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Slopes as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Slopes as simple machines.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Slopes as simple machines.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Slopes as simple machines.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Slopes as simple machines.

7. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

8. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Decomposers only
   B. Primary consumers only
   C. Tertiary consumers
   D. Producers

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Levers as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Levers as simple machines.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Levers as simple machines.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Levers as simple machines.

10. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Glucose and oxygen
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Only carbon dioxide

11. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any substance that conducts electricity
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. Any white crystal used in cooking
   D. A mixture of two liquids

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Composition of Air? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Composition of Air.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Composition of Air.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Composition of Air.

13. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Light? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Light.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Light.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Light.

14. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Overgrazing continuously

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Invertebrates? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Invertebrates.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Invertebrates.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Invertebrates.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Invertebrates.

16. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fires have no fuel
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Water always increases oxygen

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Levers as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Slopes as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Invertebrates and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Change of State and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Composition of Air and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
